statement: Off 25 C the single-salt eNRTL gives NaCl activity and osmotic coefficients far from the evaluated values, and the run says nothing. Against Archer (1992) Tables 9/10: at 373 K gamma_pm -8.0 % (0.5 m), -33.4 % (3 m), -53.8 % (6 m) and phi -4.4 %, -18.4 %, -30.5 %; at 273 K gamma_pm +5.0 %, +54.5 %, +95.8 %; at 323 K -18.7 % at 3 m. Pitzer on the same points stays within 2.1 % (gamma) and 0.7 % (phi). At 298 K eNRTL is within 3.6 %. The temperature rule is tau(T) = tau25 x 298.15/T (ENRTLSingleSalt.H:84-85), whose header calls the off-25 C result 'physical' (ENRTLSingleSalt.H:44); no eNRTL record declares a temperature range and the caveat block reads 'none raised'. In the shipped evaporator pair the same brine boils with BPE 5.200 K under Pitzer (evaporator06) and 3.945 K under eNRTL (evaporator07, ~389 K, -24 %), with no caveat naming eNRTL. Corpus reach: evaporator07 (389 K), crystalliser07 and crystalliser09 (278.15 K) run eNRTL off 25 C.

statement: Three routes read the SAME Pitzer pair records and announce temperature limits differently. A pair with NO temperature extension (96 of 99 records, e.g. Ca-Cl, Na-SO4, Mg-SO4) evaluated at 373.15 K is announced ('frozen 25 C surface used') by the pitzerActivity op only; the package route (ElectrolyteActivity, used by every process unit) and the pitzerHMW speciation route use the frozen virials silently (Pair::applyT returns without an advisory, PitzerHMW.cpp:75-100). Below the SP77 window (Na-Cl at 273 K < 273.15 K) the op and HMW announce EXTRAPOLATED; the package route does not. At the same state the two package models then disagree untold: CaCl2 3 m 373.15 K gamma_pm 0.949 (Pitzer, frozen virials) vs 0.213 (eNRTL), phi 1.681 vs 0.858. No tree measurement says which is closer. No current corpus process case is affected (its Pitzer salts NaCl/NaOH carry T data); the gap is reached by any case that declares another salt off 25 C.
evidence: finding_probes.tsv P3 (caveat counts 0 / 1 / 0 / 0 for hmw / op / pkgPitzer / pkgENRTL); announcements.tsv (pkg_Pitzer_NaCl has no 273 K line, hmw and ss_pitzer have one); item3_model_vs_model_373K.tsv

statement: PitzerForm.H:44-45 says the eNRTL/Davies kernels use 'the SAME A_phi ... (one A_phi, not two)' and EdwardsPitzer.H:72 that two models 'cannot disagree about the solvent'. Only the temperature FACTOR is shared; the 25 C anchors are four: Pitzer 0.3915 (PitzerForm.H:88), eNRTL A_DH 2.9127 = A_phi 0.39094 (ENRTLSingleSalt.H:78, ENRTLMultiSalt.H:95), Davies 0.51 (log10) = A_phi 0.39144 (AqueousActivity.cpp:131), Edwards 2.303 x 0.5108/3 = 0.39213 (EdwardsPitzer.cpp:49): a 0.3 % spread in the limiting slope.

statement: ENRTLMixedSolvent hard-codes the NaCl-water pair as 8.886 / -4.549 (ENRTLMixedSolvent.H:96) beside the catalogue's Na-Cl eNRTL 8.885 / -4.549 read by the other two eNRTL kernels, and takes A_phi from the case. At zero alcohol with A_phi 0.3915 it differs from the single-salt eNRTL by 0.04-0.12 % in gamma_pm: two homes for one parameter, small effect.

PitzerHMW::verify computes both a gamma and an osmotic (phi) single-salt oracle but returns only the gamma deviation (PitzerHMW.cpp:983), so both gates that consume it (Speciate.cpp:337-338 verifyGlobal, SpeciationSolver.cpp per-run check) never test phi; the phi number is only printed at verbosity >= 3. Today phi agrees to 1.9e-15, so nothing is wrong yet.

statement: Davies' declared band is 'trustworthy to I ~ 0.5 mol/kg' whatever the charge type. Measured against the tree's evaluated tables, gamma_pm error at the band edge is +7.7 % (NaCl, I = 0.5) and +13.0 % (KCl, I = 0.5); CaCl2 is +4.1 % at I = 0.3 and +16.7 % at I = 0.6 (announced from there on). For sulfates Davies is only usable WITH the ion-association network: Na2SO4 at I = 0.24-0.43 is -2.7 / +2.3 % with the catalogue's NaSO4- pair and +21 / +50 % without it. 'Trustworthy' at the edge overstates a 1-1 salt by up to 13 %; the beyond-band announcement itself works (66 lines in the davies probe).
